comparison.interpretation: Descriptive process-level comparisons; no significance or speedup claim. Check input, retained work, applied cadence and errors together.

analysis.decision: Inconclusive: no demonstrated benefit for this 250-client avatar workload. Small median differences and mixed paired directions; retain production code unchanged.
analysis.normalization: server_cpu_seconds_per_million_built_sends = server_cpu_cores * 1,000,000 / built_logical_avatar_work_per_second; built work is pre-transport recipient work.
analysis.validation: All eight summaries independently rederived; wrong server binary, changed worker controls and mismatched client counts rejected by real-capture tests.
analysis.tests: 19 existing tests (18 passed, one Windows-only skipped); 3 new aggregation tests passed. CodeRabbit major zero-baseline division finding fixed and covered; follow-up completed with zero findings.
analysis.raw_note: All observer, sender and global-counter CSVs retained as text. Process/readiness samples retain every field used by capture metrics and error gates. Full health snapshots, per-pair CSVs, logs, binary/source snapshots remain in ignored local captures; artifact hashes are retained.
limitations: One laptop session with four independent processes per variant, no significance test or confidence interval.
One process generates 250 logical Rust clients; only one applied-avatar observer measures 249 senders.
Applied gaps are receiver update intervals, not network RTT or end-to-end transport latency.
Dense synthetic colocated poses with fixed workers/affinity, CPU-only processing, no voice/P2P, churn or intentional network loss.
Built logical sends are pre-transport work, not UDP packet throughput.
Clock/thermal state and other user processes were not controlled continuously; diagnostics and health sampling add common overhead.
No hardware branch counters collected for this runtime experiment.
